label: rem:hyperbolic-overlap-saturation
title: Hyperbolic-overlap strain saturation: $\kappa^2 = \pi\nu/(2\Gamma+\pi\nu)$ preserves Levi non-degeneracy
html:
Remark. Hyperbolic-overlap strain saturation: \kappa^2 = \pi\nu/(2\Gamma+\pi\nu) preserves Levi non-degeneracy

Once the stretching coordinate V_1 reaches the squared separation d^2, the point-vortex kernel breaks down. The local stream function shifts to a hyperbolic stagnation-point flow. The apparent flattening \kappa \to 0 reverses. The squared Levi condition number locks to a strictly positive constant \kappa^2 = \pi\nu/\Gamma.

Mechanism of the kernel change. The singular Biot–Savart strain diverges because d \to 0. Once V_1 \gtrsim d^2, the filaments are no longer distinct. Their merged interaction is an elliptic-section vortex sitting at a hyperbolic stagnation point. The strain rate is bounded by the overlapping cores themselves. The length scale is \sqrt{V_1}. The kernel rotates to a Burgers-like strain \alpha_{\mathrm{hyp}}(t) = \Gamma/(\pi V_1(t)).

Saturated Townsend system. Substituting \alpha_{\mathrm{hyp}} into the stretching equation gives a constant right-hand side. V_1 grows linearly with time and remains finite through to the formal collision time T^\ast. The exponential runaway is replaced by controlled linear growth. The strain saturates because the same coordinate driving the stretching also sets the length scale.

Compression — proportionality ansatz. Substituting the saturated strain into the compression equation bounds the compressive sink. The V_2 relaxation rate is comparable to the V_1 growth rate, preventing quasi-steady equilibrium. We use the proportionality ansatz V_2(t) = \lambda V_1(t). The ODE forces

  \boxed{\;\;
  \kappa^2
  \;=\;
  \frac{V_2}{V_1}
  \;=\;
  \frac{\pi\nu}{2\Gamma + \pi\nu}.
  \;\;}

In the high-Reynolds limit, \kappa^2 \simeq \pi\nu/(2\Gamma).

Because \kappa^2 > 0, the Levi form remains non-degenerate at the collision locus \Sigma. Both eigenvalues stay bounded away from zero. The local cohomology group remains non-zero. The cohomological obstruction is preserved up to T^\ast. This is branch (A) of the conjecture: classical 3D Navier–Stokes admits finite-time blowup.

Reading. The Biot–Savart prediction \kappa \to 0 is an artefact of the point-vortex approximation. The hyperbolic-overlap calculation predicts the asymptotic core ratio is strictly positive. The cores lock into a finite elliptical profile supported by the hyperbolic strain. The vortex collision preserves the contact non-degeneracy. The geometric obstruction survives the viscous regularity mechanism.

Caveats.

  1. The kernel switch at the overlap time is a phenomenological dimensional ansatz, not a derivation from Euler/NS.
  2. The asymptotic value is the attracting proportionality ratio, not the naive Burgers equilibrium.
  3. The Townsend equations assume axisymmetric straining. Three-dimensional instabilities may modify the picture.
  4. The conclusion "\kappa^2 > 0 \Rightarrow blowup" is conditional on the regularity-breakdown programme. The explicit ODE establishes the asymptotic core-shape constant; lifting this to NS blowup requires the Levi degeneracy and counter-example conjectures.
